sections.html:
Clovis is the seat of Curry County, on the Llano Estacado close to the Texas line, with 38,567 residents in the 2020 census. US 60, US 70 and US 84 pass through town. Cannon Air Force Base sits roughly 7 to 8 miles west of the center. The city began in 1906 as a railroad town, and BNSF still runs a division point and a large freight yard here.

Four employers or sectors carry most of the local economy: Cannon, the rail yard, agriculture and dairy processing, and a small group of manufacturers. When one of them shifts, house sales tend to feel it.

sections.h2: Cannon Air Force Base and military sellers
sections.html:
Cannon is the largest single factor. The 27th Special Operations Wing fact sheet puts the workforce at about 6,500 military and civilian personnel at Cannon and the nearby Melrose Air Force Range. It also counts more than 7,800 military personnel, civilian employees and family members on the base population side, plus about 4,000 retirees.

Service families move on assignment cycles, so a sale tied to a permanent change of station usually runs on a fixed calendar. A buyer using a VA loan faces an appraisal and a condition review, and that can be harder for a house with a failing roof or foundation movement. A cash buyer is not tied to that review.

sections.h2: Wind, hail, snow and tornado exposure
sections.html:
Clovis has a semi-arid climate, and wind is the constant. The city sits on the southern edge of Tornado Alley, gusts often pass 30 miles per hour, and the average wind speed runs about 12 miles per hour across flat open land. Spring brings severe thunderstorms, summer evenings bring heavy rain, and snow tends to arrive for several weeks in January and February.

The town has almost no storm runoff system, so snowmelt and heavy rain can cause minor street flooding. If your lot is low or your garage floor sits near the street, buyers and inspectors will ask.

  • Roofs face wind and storm exposure all year. A financed buyer may demand fixes for lifted flashing, missing shingles or old patches.
  • Heating and cooling both matter. The normals show a January daily low near 22 degrees and a July daily high near 91 degrees.
  • Fences, sheds and carports can suffer wind damage. Note any repairs you have made.

A cash buyer prices these items into the offer and skips the repair negotiation. A listed sale usually does not.

Curry County bills in two halves, with the first due November 10 and the second due April 10. Bills go out on or before November 1, and at least half must be paid by December 10 to avoid interest and penalty.

The Assessor's Office values about 27,000 parcels of real property in the county, and taxable value is 33.33 percent of appraised value minus exemptions. Curry County is split into four school and tax districts, Clovis, Texico, Melrose and Grady, so the district serving your address affects the rate on your bill.

Taxes unpaid for more than three years can lead to transfer of the property to the State of New Mexico and sale at public auction. If you owe back taxes on a house you want to sell, raise it early with your title company, since a lien has to be paid at closing. Pull your recent bill from the Curry County Treasurer at 417 Gidding Street, Suite 150 and confirm what is open.

sections.h2: How a sale changes the tax value
sections.html:
When a Clovis house sells, the county can reset its taxable value to current market value, which often raises the next owner's bill. State statute 7-36-21.2 caps yearly increases on residential property at 3 percent over the prior year, or 6.1 percent over two years, whichever is higher. The cap does not apply in the tax year after a change of ownership.

The statute lists transfers that are not a change of ownership, including certain transfers between spouses, to a child who lives in the home, or into a revocable trust. A sale to a buyer is not on that list. A buyer comparing two houses should ask how long each owner has held the property, because a long-held house may carry a lower valuation than its price suggests.

For sellers, timing is the practical point. January 1 is the valuation date for each tax year, and title companies commonly divide the year's tax between buyer and seller at closing. Ask for that split in writing. The Assessor's Office also takes a Real Property Transfer Declaration Affidavit, and its Deeds Specialist can tell you what is needed after a deed records.

sections.h2: City rules, nuisance reports and permits
sections.html:
The city runs a 311 portal called Clovis NM Works for non-emergency problems. Neighbors can use it to report debris in alleys or overgrown lots, anonymously and with a photo. If you have an inherited or vacant house, check that no open complaint is attached to the address before you list.

Building Safety and Code Compliance sit in the same city department, and permits can be filed through the online portal. A deck, roof or electrical job done without a permit can slow a conventional sale, since a buyer's lender or inspector may ask for records. Water leaks go to Epcor Water and power outages to Xcel Energy, so collect final readings on closing day.

  • Check the city code on Municode for yard, junk vehicle and structure rules.
  • Gather permit records for any work after you bought.
  • Ask your title company about unpaid tax or utility balances.

sections.h2: Who buys in Clovis and which sale route fits
sections.html:
Buyers fall into three groups: military households, local families, and investors who rent to both. A local family may rely on a bank loan and a standard inspection. An investor or cash buyer can close faster and accept the house in its present state.

Selling on the open market can bring the highest price for a clean, updated house, but it adds showings, inspection requests, appraisal risk and commission. A cash sale gives up some price for speed and certainty. It suits probate, a move on orders, tax debt, a tenant who will not leave, or repairs the family cannot pay for.

Whichever route you take, ask for the offer in writing, ask who pays each closing cost, and have a New Mexico title company handle the closing. We do not promise a price, since any figure depends on the house, the location and the work it needs.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in Clovis?
faqs.a: It depends on title work, not on financing. A clean title can close in a matter of weeks, while liens, probate or missing signatures add time.

faqs.q: Do I owe Curry County property tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, for any tax year you owned the house on January 1 and any unpaid balance. Title companies usually collect the unpaid amount at closing.

faqs.q: Does a Clovis sale raise the property tax for the buyer?
faqs.a: Often yes. The yearly increase cap of 3 percent on residential property does not apply in the tax year after a change of ownership, so the county can value the house at current market value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clovis house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Wind and storm damage are common on the plains, and a cash buyer will usually take the house as it stands and price the roof into the offer.

faqs.q: What if the house is inherited and still in a parent's name?
faqs.a: You need legal authority to sell, which usually means probate or a court-approved personal representative in New Mexico. Talk to a New Mexico attorney first, then ask the title company what documents it needs.
